findings.problem: JobWorkflow uses status: String combined with is_validated: bool and is_sent: bool, allowing any combination of values including illegal states (e.g. status='sent' with is_sent=false, or status='pending' with is_sent=true and is_validated=true)
findings.failure_mode: Any caller can construct a JobWorkflow with contradictory lifecycle fields, breaking invariants and making reasoning about workflow correctness impossible
findings.fix: Replace status: String, is_validated: bool, is_sent: bool with a single JobStatus enum (e.g. Pending, Validated, Sent) and derive is_sent/is_validated from the enum variant

findings.problem: When a struct combines status: String, lifecycle booleans, and optional timestamps, the lifecycle must be an enum/typestate state machine so transitions are enforced at the type level
findings.failure_mode: Without an enum/typestate, invalid state transitions cannot be caught at compile time; runtime checks are needed and error-prone
findings.fix: Define a JobStatus enum with explicit variants (e.g. Pending, Validated, Sent) and encode lifecycle transitions as methods that return Result<JobWorkflow, TransitionError> or consume self and produce the next state

findings.problem: Raw primitives (String, bool, Option) enter the domain without a parse boundary/smart constructor. There is no fallible constructor enforcing domain invariants
findings.failure_mode: Callers can construct invalid states directly via JobWorkflow { id: String::from("bad"), status: "", is_validated: false, is_sent: false, sent_at_epoch_ms: None } without any validation
findings.fix: Add a private constructor with a public fallible new() method (or try_new()) that validates id is non-empty, status matches a known enum set, and lifecycle booleans are consistent with the status

findings.problem: mark_sent takes owned JobWorkflow and mutates it in place without any validation, error handling, or typestate enforcement. It accepts any status value and overwrites it to 'sent'
findings.failure_mode: A job with status='cancelled' can be overwritten to 'sent', silently allowing an invalid lifecycle transition
findings.fix: Make mark_sent a method on JobWorkflow that returns Result<JobWorkflow, TransitionError>; enforce that the current status is a transition-allowed predecessor (e.g. Validated) before allowing the transition to Sent; use the typestate enum instead of string comparison

findings.problem: Setting status via string literal ("sent") instead of an enum variant or typed constant. This is unenforceable and error-prone to typo
findings.failure_mode: Typos in status strings ('sentt', 'Sent', 'SENT') silently create inconsistent state that mark_sent won't match, and consumers can't exhaustively match
findings.fix: Replace status: String with JobStatus enum; set via enum variant assignment (e.g. self.status = JobStatus::Sent)

findings.problem: id: String is a raw primitive with no newtype wrapping or domain constraints. Empty or malformed IDs cannot be rejected at construction time
findings.failure_mode: A JobWorkflow with an empty or invalid id can be created and processed, leading to ambiguous tracking and silent data corruption
findings.fix: Wrap id in a JobId newtype with a fallible constructor (e.g. JobId::try_from(String)) that rejects empty/whitespace-only values

findings.problem: No benchmark, profiler, allocation tracking, or command evidence exists. mark_sent allocates via .to_string() on every call and creates a new String for status
findings.failure_mode: If mark_sent is called in a hot path, the redundant allocation per call is unmeasured and unbounded
findings.fix: Add a criterion or minimal benchmark for mark_sent; replace .to_string() with enum variant assignment; if status must be displayed, use Display trait on the enum

findings.problem: item.status = "sent".to_string() performs a heap allocation. No allocation budget or audit exists
findings.failure_mode: Repeated calls cause unbounded heap allocations for a status that could be represented as a zero-cost enum variant
findings.fix: Replace String status with JobStatus enum; remove to_string() call entirely

findings.problem: No dev-dependencies for testing, no benchmark section, no clippy/toml verification configuration in Cargo.toml
findings.failure_mode: No automated quality gate exists to prevent regressions
findings.fix: Add [[bench]] section for criterion benchmarks, dev-dependencies for testing, and CI-compatible clippy configuration

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for mark_sent or any performance claim
no profiler evidence (flamegraph, perf) for allocation patterns
no allocation tracking (e.g. alloc counter, jemalloc profiling)
no command evidence: cargo fmt, cargo clippy, cargo test, or cargo bench have not been run
no second-ring evidence (Kani, Miri, property tests) for state transition invariants
residual_risk: The crate has fundamental typestate and parse-boundary violations that make illegal states representable at the type level. Without enum-based JobStatus and fallible constructors, no amount of testing can guarantee lifecycle correctness. Static review only; no commands run. BLOCKER findings must be resolved before delivery.
